lines.text: In 1974, Stephen King checked into Room 217.
The Stanley Hotel, Colorado. Closing for winter. Nearly empty.
That night he dreamed of a fire hose chasing his son.
One cigarette later, he had the bones of The Shining.
But the staff tell an older story.
Chambermaid Elizabeth Wilson walks in with a lit candle.
The blast drops her through the floor, into the dining room.
Guests now report unpacked suitcases, lights switching on and off.
The legend says she's still on shift.
But the record says Elizabeth Wilson survived.
She went back to work at the hotel.
The woman said to haunt 217 didn't die in it.
And the hotel sells ghost tours.
Nobody knows. But it started like this:
